Georgia's broad-based categorical eligibility (SNAP state option;
PolicyEngine models gross screen x1.3 FPL, x2.0 for elderly/disabled
households, at 2026-01 per gov/hhs/tanf/non_cash parameters) is not in
the composed us-ga/snap/fy-2026 program, which applies only the standard
federal tests. Every selected row is verified per-row against axiom's
persisted output surface: household gross income sits inside the band
above the federal 130 percent limit the composed program applies and at
or below the state's BBCE screen, verified against axiom's own computed
gross income and limit. Axiom-side modeling boundary, tracked for
encoding in rulespec-us#1098.

Exact-household requested-month counterfactual on PolicyEngine 4.18.9 / PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3 / PolicyEngine-Core 3.30.3. The committed comparison adapter replayed over the same Case projection reproduces the report pin (Axiom 1467.0 versus January PolicyEngine 1432.699951171875), and the unmodified direct requested-month simulation reproduces the same January value. Forcing the aggregate and state TANF inputs to zero in the direct requested-month simulation produces January SNAP 1467.5; its absolute delta from Axiom, 0.5, is within the unchanged suite tolerance 7.0. The comparison bridge zeroes TANF on the Axiom input surface while PolicyEngine computes state TANF endogenously and counts it as SNAP unearned income (axiom-oracles#397 counterfactual class). Replay classifier record: class=tanf.

Disability-surface projection asymmetry, the SNAP analogue of the ssi-ecps disposition (axiom-oracles#228): the populace projection maps the Enhanced CPS is_disabled flag into Axiom's snap_member_is_elderly_or_disabled input (elderly_or_disabled transform in axiom_oracles/data/populace_input_mapping.yaml), while PolicyEngine's SNAP elderly/disabled status (has_usda_elderly_disabled) requires receipt of a disability program, which the projected input surface zeroes. Axiom therefore applies the elderly/disabled treatment (gross-test exemption and uncapped excess-shelter deduction) while PolicyEngine does not. Verified per-row on the pinned stack (PolicyEngine 4.18.9 / PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3 / PolicyEngine-Core 3.30.3): the committed adapter reproduces the report values; the direct January simulation shows has_usda_elderly_disabled false while the persisted Axiom input surface carries the elderly/disabled flag for an under-60 member (1 cases / 2 rows).

Self-employment loss pass-through: the projection's flat 0.6 self-employment netting (axiom_oracles/data/populace_input_mapping.yaml) passes Enhanced CPS self-employment losses through as negative Axiom earned income (sample ecps-65250: persisted snap_gross_monthly_earned_income -64573.42), while PolicyEngine floors SNAP self-employment income at zero (snap_self_employment_income_after_expense_deduction takes max(., 0)). Axiom's income tests pass on the loss-netted surface and it awards a benefit while PolicyEngine remains ineligible or lower. Verified per-row on the pinned stack (PolicyEngine 4.18.9 / PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3 / PolicyEngine-Core 3.30.3): the committed adapter reproduces the report values, and every selected row carries a negative Axiom earned-income input while the January PolicyEngine earned income is floored at or above zero (3 cases / 5 rows). A dedicated tracking issue for the self-employment-loss netting in the Populace bridge still needs filing; axiom-oracles#397 documents the same unequal-cross-program-input policy problem (same linkage as the fl-snap-ecps se-loss-netting class).

The comparison's PolicyEngine eligibility boolean comes from the batch output dataset's calendar-2026 aggregation, which reports eligible although the direct requested-month (2026-01) simulation is ineligible for January: the household fails the January income eligibility tests under the FY-2026 parameters while other 2026 months pass (income-limit uprating across the October fiscal-year boundary), and Axiom evaluates 2026-01 only. Verified per-row on the pinned stack (PolicyEngine 4.18.9 / PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3 / PolicyEngine-Core 3.30.3): the committed adapter reproduces the annual-aggregated True while the direct January simulation returns False on every selected row (2 rows; sample ecps-30869 January gross-income-to-poverty ratio 1.3263). The January benefit is zero on both engines, so only the eligibility boolean diverges — a harness period-aggregation artifact, not an engine defect.

Unmapped state-vocabulary shelter input (the CA PUB-275 population-input bridge class): the composed us-ga/snap/fy-2026 program derives snap_total_allowable_shelter_expenses from the state-manual input monthly_allowable_shelter_costs, which matches neither populace mapping rule (household_shelter_costs_incurred / snap_total_allowable_shelter_expenses in axiom_oracles/data/populace_input_mapping.yaml), so the generic projector defaults the unmapped input to zero and Axiom computes a zero excess-shelter deduction, while PolicyEngine deducts shelter from the same household's Enhanced CPS housing cost. Verified per-row on the pinned stack (PolicyEngine 4.18.9 / PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3 / PolicyEngine-Core 3.30.3): the committed adapter reproduces the report values, PolicyEngine's January excess-shelter deduction is positive, Axiom's persisted surface carries neither a shelter input nor an excess-shelter deduction output, and every residual reconciles as 0.3x the net-income gap between the two surfaces within the 30-percent rounding (19 cases / 19 rows; sample ecps-29900: PE shelter deduction 426.6, Axiom net 614.31 vs PE net 187.05). Population-input bridge artifact; a mapping rule for the state vocabulary still needs filing.

Reverified on PolicyEngine 4.18.9 / PolicyEngine-US 1.767.3 / PolicyEngine-Core 3.30.3. Exact-household requested-month replay: PolicyEngine's January snap_earned_income is 0 for this all-minor household (ages [13]) although the projected Case carries the member's wages — PolicyEngine excludes all earnings of an imputed K-12 member age 17 or younger without requiring the co-resident-parent or parental-control condition in 7 CFR 273.9(c)(7). The sole-minor household is valid under 273.1(a)(1), but its wages count under 273.9(b)(1)(i), so Axiom correctly fails the income gate and returns zero benefit while PolicyEngine pays 298 (January replay 298).
